newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX in talks with IPE on cross-margining.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX in talks with IPE on cross-margining.

text.p: New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) is in talks with London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on a cross-margining agreement for crude trading, an exchange source said.

The agreement would allow a lower margin for trading across the two exchange's products. For example, trading a spread between West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude would cost a dealer less since part of the risk would already be offset by the spread itself.
"The talks are very preliminary, and we don't know what the formation of the agreement would be if there were one," said the source who requested anonymity.
The talks occurred among high-level exchange executives during a series of oil industry gatherings in London last week dubbed "IPE week," said the source.
NYMEX already offers lower margins for inter-commodity trading, such as between gold and silver.
The current NYMEX margin for crude is $1,500 for clearing members; $1,650 for members; and $2,025 for customers.
